name: Deutsche Umwelthilfe (DUH) – Diesel Bans
description: Actions brought by the NGO Deutsche Umwelthilfe (DUH) against the Länder of Baden-Württemberg (Stuttgart) and Nordrhein-Westfalen (Düsseldorf) over the continued exceedance of the annual NO2 limit value in numerous German cities. At issue was whether the air quality plans in force complied with Directive 2008/50/EC and the Bundes-Immissionsschutzgesetz and whether it was lawful to impose traffic bans on diesel vehicles.
outcome: The Bundesverwaltungsgericht held that traffic bans (Fahrverbote) on diesel vehicles are permissible by way of exception: where they are the only suitable measure to comply “in the shortest possible time” with the EU NO2 limits, they must be adopted, subject to proportionality (phased introduction, no bans on Euro 5 diesel vehicles before 1 September 2019, exemptions). Low-emission zones (Umweltzonen) had existed since 2008; following the judgment, diesel bans were introduced in a few cities (Hamburg, Stuttgart, Darmstadt, Berlin, Munich), while in Frankfurt the ban never entered into force, having been annulled by the Hessian Higher Administrative Court (VGH Kassel) on 10 December 2019.
